==English== [[Image:20060513 toolbox.jpg|thumb|Several tools in a toolbox]] ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*dewh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|tool}}, {{m|enm|tol}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tōl|t=tool, implement, instrument|lit=that with which one prepares something}}, perhaps borrowed from {{der|en|non|tól}}, but at any rate ultimately from {{der|en|gem-pro|*tōlą|t=that which is used in preparation, tool}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dewh₂-|t=to tie to, secure}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|taw|t1=to prepare|le|id2=agent noun}} {{gloss|agent suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|tuil||tool, implement, instrument, device}}, {{cog|is|tól||tool}}, {{cog|fo|tól||tool, instrument}}. Related to {{cog|ang|tāwian||to make, prepare, or cultivate}}; see {{l|en|taw}}, and {{l|en|tow}} ("fibres used for spinning").{{cite-book|last=Carus|first=Paul|title=The philosophy of the tool|publisher=The Open Court Publishing Company|pages=3-4|location=Chicago|year=1893}}{{cite-book|last=Hall|first=John Richard Clark|others=Supplement by Herbert D. Merritt|title=A Concise Anglo-Saxon Dictionary|publisher=Cambridge University Press|pages=338 & 345|year=1960|year_published=1984|edition=4|isbn=9780802065483}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|to͞ol}} * {{IPA|en|/tuːl/|a=England,Wales}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-tool.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{IPA|en|/tul/|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/tʉːl/|a=General Australian}} * {{IPA|en|/tʉl/|a=Scotland,NI}} * {{rhymes|en|uːl|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|tulle}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|Q39546}} Any physical [[device]] meant to ease or do a [[task]]. #: {{hypo|en|hand tool|power tool|machine tool|;|Thesaurus:tool}} #: {{ux|en|Several prehistoric '''tools''', including a stone ax, were found during the dig.}} #: {{ux|en|A screwdriver is a '''tool''' that no household should be without.}} #: {{ux|en|A stapler is a '''tool''' for attaching papers to others.}} ## Any piece of [[equipment]] used in a profession, such as a [[craftsman]]'s. ##: {{hypo|en|hand tool|power tool|machine tool|;|Thesaurus:tool}} ##: {{collocation|en|the '''tools''' of the trade}} ##: {{ux|en|Rakes, shovels, hoes, and spades are some of the '''tools''' of the gardener's trade.}} ##: {{ux|en|I don't have the right '''tools''' to start fiddling around with the engine.}} ##: {{ux|en|A timing light is a '''tool''' that only an automotive mechanic, professional or amateur, would have.}} # Anything that aids someone to perform an operation; an [[instrument]]; a [[means]]. #: {{ux|en|Idleness is a '''tool''' of the devil.}} #: {{ux|en|A spreadsheet app and a bookkeeping app are some of the principal '''tools''' of a bookkeeper.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1867|title=The Masonic Trowel|volume=6|page=44 |passage=What was the need of a man to do that? "One stick at a time;" if Ned could not do that, he was a poor '''tool'''. Ah, a poor '''tool''' he proved to be.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=July-August|author=Catherine Clabby|magazine=w:American Scientist|title=Focus on Everything|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/4/focus-on-everything|passage=Not long ago, it was difficult to produce photographs of tiny creatures with every part in focus.{{...}}A photo processing technique called focus stacking has changed that. Developed as a '''tool''' to electronically combine the sharpest bits of multiple digital images, focus stacking is a boon to biologists seeking full focus on a micron scale.|accessdate=16 September 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170511100905/http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/4/focus-on-everything|archivedate=11 May 2017}} # {{lb|en|computing}} A piece of [[software]] used to develop software or hardware, or to perform low-level operations. #: {{hyper|en|application|program}} #: {{hypo|en|utility|applet}} #: {{ux|en|The software engineer had been developing lots of EDA '''tools'''.}} #: {{ux|en|a '''tool''' for recovering deleted files from a disk}} # A person or group which is used or controlled, usually [[unwittingly]], by another person or group, a [[pawn]]. #: {{ux|en|She was a '''tool''' of the pharmaceutical lobby.}} #: {{ux|en|He was a '''tool''' of a foreign influence operation.}} # {{lb|en|baseball}} A particular [[skill#Noun|skill]] pertaining to [[baseball#Noun|baseball]] (such as [[hitting#Noun|hitting]], [[running#Noun|running]], etc.). #: {{ux|en|a five-'''tool''' player}} #* {{quote-web|en|author=Mark Bechtel|title="there's Something Fun About Yooouuuk"|work=w:Sports Illustrated|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081014071400/http://vault.sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1115795/index.htm|date=7 November 2007|passage=When asked what he liked about Youk [{{w|Kevin Youkilis}}], former Boston scout Matt Haas says, "At first glance, not a lot." (Mind you, this is one of the few scouts who actually wanted the kid.) "He was unorthodox," says Haas, who now scouts for the Arizona Diamondbacks. "He had an extreme crouch—his thighs were almost parallel to the ground. And he was heavier than he is now. But the more I watched him, the more I just thought, Throw the '''tools''' out the window. This guy can play baseball."}} # {{lb|en|vulgar|informal}} A [[penis]], notably with a sexual or erotic connotation. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:penis}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 8|act=V|scene=iv|page=231|passage=Or haue wee some strange Indian with the great '''''Toole''''', come to Court, the women so besiege vs?}} # {{lb|en|by extension|vulgar|slang|pejorative}} An obnoxious or uptight person. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:jerk}} #: {{hypo|en|power tool}} #: {{ux|en|He won't sell us tickets because it's 3:01, and they went off sale at 3.
